title: Egg Salad with Light Italian Dressing

content.title: About
content.content: Egg salad with light Italian dressing is a classic dish made from hard‑boiled eggs, finely chopped vegetables, and a dressing of olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice and aromatic Italian herbs. The recipe first appeared in 1962 and quickly became popular for its light, refreshing flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first published recipe showed up in U.S. cooking magazines in 1962.
The light Italian dressing typically includes oregano, basil and garlic, giving the salad a distinct Mediterranean aroma.
Egg salad is often used as a filling for sandwiches and wraps.
Variations may add celery, scallions or capers for extra bite.
The dish stays fresh in the refrigerator for up to 3 days, making it convenient for make‑ahead meals.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs provide a complete source of protein essential for tissue repair and muscle maintenance.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Olive‑oil‑based dressing supplies monounsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs are rich in B12, riboflavin and folate, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Herbs and lemon juice add vitamin C and polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Digestive ease
items.content: A light dressing without mayonnaise reduces saturated fat content, making the salad easier on the stomach.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to egg proteins and must avoid the dish.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improperly cooked or stored eggs can harbor salmonella; always fully hard‑boil eggs and keep the salad refrigerated.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume in moderation.

items.title: Acidic dressing
items.content: Vinegar and lemon juice may irritate the stomach of those with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish, alongside bread or crackers, or use it as a sandwich filling. Garnish with fresh herbs, cherry tomatoes or olives for extra color.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Add a splash of fresh dressing before serving if needed to refresh the flavor.
